newsitem.title: USA: LIPA board approves partial Lilco takeover.
newsitem.headline: LIPA board approves partial Lilco takeover.

text.p: The 15-member board of the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) has voted to approve the partial takeover of Long Island Lighting Co assets, LIPA said Tuesday.

The Monday vote clears the way for review of the plan by the Public Authorities Control Board, a three-member panel comprised of New York State Gov. George Pataki, Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno and State Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver.

LIPA's approval comes amid a host of public hearings on the matter, six of which were conducted by LIPA. A hearing by the New York Assembly Energy Committee, featuring the testimony of LIPA Chairman Richard Kessel, is to be held by the New York Assembly Energy Committee at 1100 EDT/1500 GMT today.
Key elements of the plan are a LIPA takeover of Lilco's transmission and distribution system, most regulatory assets, and Lilco's share of the Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear power plant.
The takeover will be paid for through a stock purchase from a Brooklyn Union Gas /Lilco holding company, financed in part by a proposed $7.3 billion in municipal bond sales.

Under the plan, LIPA said, electric rates on Long Island will be reduced more than 20 percent within the first five years of implementation. Ratepayers in Nassau and Suffolk counties will receive rate cuts of 18.2 percent and 16.4 percent, respectively.
In addition, the plan would resolve the $1.2 billion tax overassessment case brought by Lilco against Nassau and Suffolk counties, LIPA said.

"The LIPA process must move forward," said LIPA Chairman Kessel. "It's time to lower electric rates on Long Island and to protect property owners from onerous tax increases that could be triggered by the court-ordered Shoreham tax case and other pending tax certiorari cases."

The trustees also approved provisions that would allow for additional changes in the takeover plan reflecting changes suggested by the public and elected officials. Prospective changes, which LIPA did not identify, would be negotiated with Lilco and Brooklyn Union and brought back to the LIPA board for final approval.
